lab2.explanation: The weak hash maps any input to one of only 256 values, so collisions are guaranteed by the pigeonhole principle and trivial to find by brute force. A hash function used in a blockchain must be collision resistant, otherwise an attacker could swap one transaction for another without changing the block hash. SHA-256 has a 256-bit output and no known practical collision attack, which is why it is used for transaction IDs, Merkle roots and proof-of-work.
